why.title: Why a Bank Robber Covered His Face in Lemon Juice
why.why: It uses extreme human absurdity as a narrative hook to explain a complex cognitive bias (Dunning-Kruger Effect) in an entertaining, story-driven format.

why.title: She Made Half Her Class Feel Inferior in Just One Day #shorts
why.why: It leverages high emotional tension and social experiment storytelling to create an immediate curiosity gap about psychological manipulation.

why.title: Your Brain Has a Door Problem
why.why: It frames a mundane everyday experience (the 'Doorway Effect' memory lapse) into a surprising, highly relatable physical anomaly of the brain.

hook_patterns: Bizarre historical anecdote framed as a bizarre life hack
Hyper-relatable daily glitch framed as a 'brain defect'
High-stakes social experiment starting at the dramatic climax
todays_angle: Translate absurd real-world psychological phenomena into chaotic, relatable banter between Leo and Mia.

ideas.title: The Lemon Juice Robber (Dunning-Kruger Effect)
ideas.concept: Leo shows up to rob Mia's apartment wearing invisible ink (lemon juice) on his face because he read it online. Mia has to calmly explain the Dunning-Kruger effect while Leo gets progressively more confused about why she can still see him.

ideas.title: Why You Forget Things In Doorways (The Doorway Effect)
ideas.concept: Mia walks into the kitchen to tell Leo something urgent, stops dead in the doorway, and forgets everything. Leo panics thinking the room wiped her memory, leading to an animated breakdown of how the brain creates 'event boundaries'.

ideas.title: The Fake Eye Contact Hack (Pygmalion Effect)
ideas.concept: Mia convinces Leo that looking at someone's forehead makes them think you're a genius. Leo tries it on Mia during lunch, causing an escalating standoff of psychological mind games.

avoid: Generic text-on-screen voiceover summaries without character interaction
Overused '4 Mindsets to Win' motivational speech style formats
